videos.name: tour
videos.title: A first look
videos.summary: A walk from the sign-in picker through the home page, the position grid, one deal and the quarterly monitoring board.

steps.text: The prototype signs in with a picker of synthetic users. Each one holds a role.
Home: invested capital, NAV and returns for the positions this user may see.
What needs attention comes first: watchlist flags and capital notices that are due.
Exposure and the NAV trend, from Locked valuations only.
The portfolio: every position in one grid.
Search, filter by deal type, or export the grid to CSV.
Opening a row shows the one-pager for that deal.
The one-pager: invested capital, current NAV, gross MOIC and gross IRR.
Financial performance for the latest quarter, with the prior year beside it when it is on record.
Back to the portfolio, and on to the monitoring board.
Monitoring: for each active position, whether the quarterly report is in, read and approved.
Each row links to the report, the extraction run and the approval.

videos.name: valuation
videos.title: A valuation, from draft to lock
videos.summary: Operations starts and prepares a valuation, the deal team approves it, an approver locks it, and the version screen shows the lock text and its hash.

steps.text: The valuation board. One active position has no mark for this quarter yet.
Operations starts a draft: the position, the method and the fair value.
Operations prepares it.
Next, the deal team. The person who prepared a valuation can never approve it.
Last, an approver selects the version and locks it from the batch bar.
The version screen shows what the lock covers.
The lock is a SHA-256 hash over the version, the method, its inputs and the fair value.
Three decisions by three different people.
Reports read Locked valuations only. A correction reopens one into a new version.

videos.name: capital-call
videos.title: A capital call with a changed wire
videos.summary: A capital call arrives with new wire instructions: operations reviews it and drafts the ticket, the release stays blocked until a second person verifies the change by callback, and a third person approves.

steps.text: Capital activity: calls, distributions and payments, with alerts as due dates approach.
This capital call is due in two days and is marked Wire change.
Two alerts: the wire instructions changed, and the notice presses for a quick payment.
Operations reviews the call and drafts the trade ticket.
The release is blocked. The wire changed inside the hold window, and a preparer cannot approve their own ticket.
A second operations person opens the proposed instruction in the wire register.
They call back on a number sourced independently, and record the result.
The new version is verified and active. The earlier one is superseded.
Inside the hold window the release needs a third person: an approver who touched neither step.
The ticket is approved against the verified instruction. Bank details stay masked outside the wire register.

videos.name: deal
videos.title: A deal, from pipeline to position
videos.summary: A deal passes the diligence gate and the investment committee, its closing shows the commitment and the client breakdown, and it becomes a position in the portfolio.

steps.text: The pipeline: every deal by stage. This one is in diligence.
The gate: no investment committee while a required task is open.
The deal team completes the required tasks.
An approver takes it to committee and records the decision.
Operations opens the closing with one close date.
The allocation leads with the commitment and the amount received against it.
Client lines sit beneath their vehicle, in a breakdown that opens on request.
Documents received, allocations tied: operations confirms the closing.
The deal closes and becomes a position. It carries no figure yet: nothing is invented.

videos.name: documents
videos.title: From a sponsor report to the record
videos.summary: Operations indexes the document store, a batch reads the quarterly reports, a reviewer checks a value against its page and approves, and the figures appear on the position with their source.

steps.text: The document hub starts empty. Operations indexes the document store.
Each file is hashed, tagged by a classifier and linked to its deal or fund.
A tag below the confidence threshold waits in the review queue for a person.
Extraction: a batch reads the financial reports of the quarter.
In the prototype a mock model answers. Each run waits for a reviewer.
Every value in a run carries its page, a short quote and a confidence.
Click a value to see where it was read: the page, with the quote highlighted.
Clean values are accepted in one go. Flagged ones are decided one by one.
The reviewer approves with a reason. Nothing reaches the record before this.
The deal team now reads the quarter on the position.
The approved figures link back to the document and the page they came from.

videos.name: value-creation
videos.title: Value creation and entry metrics
videos.summary: The gain on the equity and continuation vehicle positions split by driver, the bridge opened into revenue and margin, valuation growth against EBITDA growth on enterprise value, a filter to one vehicle, the entry metric bands, and one company’s value creation card.

steps.text: Analytics, Value creation: the gain on equity and continuation vehicle positions.
The tiles split it by driver: EBITDA growth, multiple expansion, debt paydown, and mark and timing.
A bridge walks from invested capital to value now.
A switch opens EBITDA growth into revenue growth and margin change.
Each company: valuation growth against its EBITDA growth since entry.
Measured here on enterprise value, the like-for-like view.
A filter to one vehicle. Every figure is rolled up again over its positions.
Entry metrics keeps the filter: performance by entry purchase multiple band and by entry net leverage band.
Back on Value creation, a company in the table opens its deal.
On the deal’s Performance tab, the value creation card shows the bridge for that one company.
